authors: Paoul S. Martinez, Caryn E. Plummer
title: Ophthalmology of Crocodilia: Alligators, Crocodiles, Caimans, and Gharials

authors: April R. Beatty, Mark Flint, Jaylene B. Flint, Anne J. Gemensky‐Metzler, Dubraska V. Diaz-Campos, Joany C. van Balen et al.

journal: Journal of Zoo and Wildlife Medicine
why: Pupil diameter and dilation in 165 juvenile American alligators, the only large measured sample of Alligator mississippiensis eyes.

authors: André Tavares Somma, Leandro Lima, Rogério Ribas Lange, Amália Turner Giannico, Fabiano Montiani‐Ferreira

title: Light and electron microscopy of the photoreceptors in the retina of the red‐eared slider, Pseudemys scripta elegans
why: Photoreceptor types of the red-eared slider retina, to confirm the number of cone classes.

title: Spectral sensitivity of the freshwater turtle Pseudemys script a elegans: Evidence for the filter-effect of colored oil droplets
why: Spectral sensitivity of the red-eared slider and the filter effect of its coloured oil droplets.

title: Turtles (Pseudemys nelsoni) learn about visual cues indicating food from experienced turtles.
why: Behavioural test of what Florida redbelly turtles (Pseudemys nelsoni) learn from visual cues, a species of its own in north Florida.

title: Long-term retention of visual tasks by two species of emydid turtles, Pseudemys nelsoni and Trachemys scripta.
why: Visual discrimination retained by Pseudemys nelsoni and Trachemys scripta over months.

title: Visual pigments of frog and tadpole (Rana pipiens)
why: Visual pigments of Rana pipiens as adult and tadpole, for the leopard frog's own pigment values.

why: Rana temporaria visual pigment measurements by hydroxylamine bleaching, for the common European frog.

title: Visual performance of the toad (Bufo bufo) at low light levels: retinal ganglion cell responses and prey-catching accuracy

why: Survey of pupil shape across frogs and toads including North American treefrogs and bullfrogs, to settle the horizontal pupil assumption.

title: Insights into the evolution of photoreceptor oil droplets in frogs and toads

title: Differences in ocular media transmittance in classical frog and toad model species and its impact on visual sensitivity

title: Recurrent evolution of ultraviolet vision in frogs and toads is linked to transitions in locomotor mode.

title: Visual optics in toads (Bufo americanus)

why: Photoreceptor types and distribution in the cane toad retina.

title: Retinal ganglion cell distribution and spatial resolution in the Asiatic toad Bufo gargarizans (Günther, 1859)
why: Ganglion cell map and acuity in the Asiatic toad, a measured Bufo for the spatial resolution row.

title: Flicker fusion characteristics of rod photoreceptors in the toad
why: Flicker fusion of toad rods (Bufo marinus), to check the cane toad flicker figure against its source.

title: The Visual Field of a North-African toad Bufo mauritanicus
why: Visual field of a North African toad Bufo mauritanicus, to extend the field of view figure.
